lessons.title: What Is Chinese New Year?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say that Chinese New Year is a celebration marked by many Chinese families and communities.
lessons.starter_activity: Show pictures of Chinese New Year celebrations (lanterns, dragon dance).
lessons.main_activity: Discuss simply what Chinese New Year celebrates and how families/communities celebrate.
key_questions: What do you see in these pictures?
How do families celebrate?

differentiation.extension: Compare to another festival learned about this year

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cultural awareness — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap key Chinese New Year facts.
lessons.home_link: Talk about festivals your family celebrates.

lessons.title: Making a Chinese Lantern
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a simple paper lantern craft.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at real/picture examples of Chinese lanterns.
lessons.main_activity: Children make a simple folded paper lantern, decorating with bright colours.
key_questions: What colours have you used?
How does your lantern hang?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor skill and creative choice — evidence for EAD.1/PD.2.
lessons.home_link: Look at lanterns/decorations at home or in pictures.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'The Great Race' (Chinese Zodiac Story)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name at least two animals from the Chinese zodiac story.
lessons.main_activity: Read the story of the Great Race, discussing the animals and the order they finished.
key_questions: Which animal came first?
Which animals do you remember?

differentiation.extension: Recall the order of several animals

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and recall — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the order of animals in the race.
lessons.home_link: Find out which zodiac animal represents your birth year with family.

lessons.title: The Dragon Dance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what happens during a dragon dance celebration.
lessons.starter_activity: Watch a short video clip or look at pictures of a dragon dance.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss why dragon dances are performed at Chinese New Year (good luck, celebration) and what children notice about the costume/movement.
key_questions: What do you notice about the dragon costume?
Why do people perform this dance?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note cultural observation and description — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap what a dragon dance is for.
lessons.home_link: Look up a video of a dragon dance together if possible.

lessons.title: Dragon Dance Movement
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move together cooperatively representing a dragon.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the dragon dance discussion from Monday/Tuesday morning.
lessons.main_activity: Children hold a long fabric/paper dragon puppet together and practise moving in a wiggling, cooperative line to music.
resources_needed: Long fabric or paper dragon puppet, music
key_questions: How do you move together as a dragon?
What happens if one part moves too fast?

differentiation.extension: Child leads the dragon's head movement

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe cooperative movement and coordination — evidence for EAD.2/PSED.3/PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Perform the dragon dance for another group.
lessons.home_link: Make a simple dragon puppet together at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'sh' Digraph
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the digraph sound 'sh' and blend words (ship, shop, shed).
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'sh' digraph sound/action; blend new words.
key_questions: What sound do these two letters make?
Can you blend sh-o-p?

lessons.title: Chinese New Year Food and Family Gatherings
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how sharing food brings families together at Chinese New Year.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss foods children share with family at celebrations.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss/look at pictures of Chinese New Year family reunion meals, noting the importance of family gathering together.
resources_needed: Chinese New Year food/family picture cards
key_questions: Why do families gather together to eat?
What foods do you share with your family?

differentiation.extension: Compare to own family gathering traditions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cultural understanding — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the importance of family gatherings.
lessons.home_link: Share a meal or gathering tradition with your family this week.

lessons.title: Making Red Envelope Decorations
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to decorate a simple envelope/card craft.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at real/picture examples of red envelopes (hongbao).
lessons.main_activity: Children decorate a red paper envelope/card template with gold patterns, discussing that red and gold represent luck.
key_questions: What colours are you using?
Why are red and gold used?

differentiation.extension: Design own envelope shape and pattern

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor and colour symbolism understanding — evidence for EAD.1/UTW.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about lucky colours or symbols in your own family's traditions.

lessons.title: Writing 'Happy New Year' Cards
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple greeting message.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at an example greeting card.
lessons.main_activity: Children design and attempt to write 'Happy New Year' on a card using known phonics sounds.
key_questions: What does your card say?
Can you write 'happy'?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note purposeful writing attempt — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.home_link: Make a greeting card for someone at home.

lessons.title: Comparing New Year Celebrations
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare Chinese New Year to the New Year celebration learned about in Week 15.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and compare how Chinese New Year and 1 January New Year are similar (fresh start, celebration) and different (timing, traditions).
key_questions: What is similar about these celebrations?
What is different?

differentiation.support: Point to one similarity with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative reasoning across cultural topics — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of similarities and differences found.
lessons.home_link: Talk about different new year celebrations your family knows about.

lessons.title: Chinese New Year Song and Dance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to join in with a simple Chinese New Year themed song/rhyme with actions.
lessons.starter_activity: Listen to a simple Chinese New Year song.
lessons.main_activity: Learn simple actions/movements to a Chinese New Year song, practising with increasing confidence.
key_questions: What action goes with this line?
How does the music make you feel?

differentiation.extension: Suggest and lead a new action

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe participation and expressive movement — evidence for EAD.2.

lessons.title: Retelling the Great Race Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell key parts of the Chinese zodiac story.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards of the zodiac animals, children retell parts of the race in order.
key_questions: Which animal came first? Second?
How did they get across the river?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Chinese New Year Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about Chinese New Year learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Chinese New Year' display combining lanterns, red envelopes, and zodiac learning.
key_questions: What have we learned about Chinese New Year?
What was your favourite part?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about Chinese New Year with your family.

lessons.title: Chinese New Year Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to perform the dragon dance and song together as a celebration.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance combining the dragon dance movement and the song, with lanterns and decorations displayed.
resources_needed: Craft from the week, dragon puppet, music player
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
How did it feel to perform together?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence, cooperation, and enjoyment — evidence for EAD.2/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the festival week.
lessons.home_link: Perform the dragon dance for family this weekend.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: 'ch' and 'sh' Digraphs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read words using the 'ch' and 'sh' digraphs.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations: word-building with both digraphs, reading cards, simple sentence reading (e.g. 'the ship has chips').
key_questions: Can you build and read this word?
Can you read this sentence?

differentiation.support: Build/read simple digraph words with support
differentiation.extension: Read sentences with both digraphs independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Finalise week 18 digraph phonics tracker for 'ch' and 'sh'.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate both digraphs learned with a reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading words with 'ch' and 'sh' over the weekend.
